region.zh: 伊甸平原，兩河流域上游（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Genesis 1-2, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 1-2

summary.en: Over six days God calls light, sky, land, plants, sun and moon, animals, and finally humanity — male and female in his own image — out of a formless, watery deep; he surveys it all as very good and hallows the seventh day of rest. For Christian readers the Spirit moving on the waters is read as the Spirit of God active in creation.
summary.zh: 六日之中，神自幽暗深淵依次造出光、穹蒼、大地、草木、日月、走獸，末造人類——按神形像造男造女；神觀其所造盡皆甚好，並定第七日為聖。基督徒讀之，見神的靈運行水面，參贊化育。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Christianity (and Judaism). Presented as a comparative cosmogony alongside other creation narratives — a scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters. And God said, Let there be light: and there was light. And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth. So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.

Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them. And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.

title.en: The Garden of Eden and the First Marriage

region.en: Eden, by the four-headed river (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸園，四河之源（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Genesis 2, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 2

summary.en: The LORD God shapes Adam from dust, breathes life into him, plants Eden with its two fateful trees, and gives him the first command; naming every beast shows him that no partner is found — so God builds Eve from Adam's rib, and the first marriage charter is spoken.
summary.zh: 耶和華神以塵土造亞當，吹生氣使其活；植伊甸園，立二樹，賜首誡。為野地走獸命名之際，配偶終不可得，神遂取亞當之肋骨造夏娃；人要離開父母，與妻子連合，二人成為一體。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The rib-birth and marriage charter are presented as a comparative narrative of humans molded from earth.

passages.text: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul. And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed. And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.

And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it. And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.

And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; and the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man. And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.

title.en: The Fall: Serpent, Fruit, and Exile

region.en: Eden, the tree in the midst (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸園，園中樹下（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Genesis 3, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 3

summary.en: The subtle serpent persuades Eve that eating the forbidden fruit brings godlike knowledge instead of death; she and Adam eat, their eyes are opened, and shame arrives. Curses fall on serpent, woman, and ground, and a flaming sword closes Eden — in Christian reading the moment death, toil, and the promise of the woman's seed bruising the serpent's head enter the world.
summary.zh: 狡蛇誘夏娃：食禁果者眼目明亮，如神能知善惡。二人食之，赤裸知羞；蛇、女、地皆受咒詛，耕作汗顏，死亡入世。基於第三章十五節「女人後裔將傷蛇首」，基督教讀之為原始福音，而基路伯與火劍封閉生命樹之路。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Presented as the Hebrew-Christian origin-of-death narrative; serpent imagery tagged as world-serpent is an interpretive act, noted here.

passages.text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden? And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die: for God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil. And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

And the LORD God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life: and I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel. Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children. And unto Adam he said, cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever: therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken. So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

title.en: Cain and Abel: The First Death

region.en: Field east of Eden, land of Nod (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊甸東野，流浪之地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Genesis 4, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 4

summary.en: God respects Abel's firstling offering but not Cain's fruit of the ground; sin crouches at the door, and in the field Cain kills his brother — the first death in scripture. Cursed from the earth, marked so none may slay him, Cain wanders east of Eden; Abel's blood crying from the ground became a Christian figure of innocent blood and of the founder of the 'city of man'.
summary.zh: 神悅納亞伯羊羔之祭，不納該隱地裏所出；罪伏於門前，該隱怒而殺弟——聖經首樁死亡。該隱受詛咒漂流，得七倍之護佑記號。其血從地裏哀告，基督教傳統以之喻義人之血，而該隱建城，被解讀為人之城之濫觴。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Christianity and Judaism. Included as the canonical origin-of-death narrative; scholarly framing only.

passages.text: And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering: but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell. And the LORD said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.

And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. And the LORD said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper? And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground. And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother's blood from thy hand; when thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.

And Cain said unto the LORD, My punishment is greater than I can bear. Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and it shall come to pass, that every one that findeth me shall slay me. And the LORD said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him. And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

title.en: The Line of Cain: Shepherds, Singers, Smiths
title.zh: 該隱之系：牧者、歌者、鐵匠

region.en: Land of Nod, city of Enoch (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 流浪之地，以諾城（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Genesis 4, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 4

summary.en: In Cain's exiled line the arts of civilization are founded: Enoch builds the first city, Jabal the tents and cattle of herders, Jubal the harp and organ of music, Tubalcain the forging of brass and iron — while Lamech's boast of a blood-vengeance seventy-sevenfold darkens the lineage. In Christian tradition this culture-registry is shadowed by the city of man, set against the line of Seth that began to call on the name of the LORD.
summary.zh: 文明之藝起於該隱流放之系：以諾築首城，雅八創畜牧帳棚，猶八創琴瑟之音，土八該隱冶銅打鐵；而拉麥誇口復仇七十七倍，血染世系。基督教釋經以人之城對照塞特之系——彼時人才求告耶和華的名。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The inventor catalogue is presented as an etiological genealogy of the crafts.

passages.text: And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch. And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle. And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ. And Zillah, she also bare Tubalcain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron.

And Lamech said unto his wives, Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice; ye wives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: for I have slain a man to my wounding, and a young man to my hurt. If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold. And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: for God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew. And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.

title.en: Enoch Walked with God, and Was Not
title.zh: 以諾與神同行，不見於世

region.en: The patriarchal line of Seth (symbolic pin)

texts.period: Genesis 5 with Jude 14-15, Genesis c. 6th-5th century BCE; Jude 1st century CE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Genesis 5 and Jude 1

summary.en: Amid the nine-hundred-year patriarchs of Genesis 5, Enoch alone walks with God, lives 365 years, and simply 'was not; for God took him' — scripture's first bodily translation to heaven. Christian tradition made him the archetype of the rapture, and the Epistle of Jude quotes Enoch as a prophet foretelling the Lord's coming with ten thousands of his saints.
summary.zh: 創世記譜系中壽數近千的族長之間，唯以諾與神同行三百年，三百六十五歲而「不見於世，因神取了他去」——聖經首位活升天者。基督教傳統以之為被提原型；猶大書更引以諾為先知，預言主偕萬聖降臨。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The translation of Enoch is presented alongside other taken-up narratives.

passages.text: And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: and Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: and all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: and Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.

And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, to execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

title.en: Sons of God and the Nephilim

region.zh: 洪水前之世界（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Genesis 6:1-4, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 6

summary.en: When humanity multiplies, the 'sons of God' take the daughters of men as wives, and their children are the Nephilim — the giants, mighty men of old, men of renown. With this mixing of the divine and human orders God limits the human span to 120 years; Christian interpretive tradition (building on 1 Enoch) read the sons of God as fallen angels, the Watchers who taught forbidden arts and fathered the giants.
summary.zh: 人類繁衍之際，神之子見人之女子美，遂娶為妻；其子即拿非利——上古英武有名之巨人。神於是將人的年日限為一百二十年。基督教釋經（承《以諾一書》）視「神之子」為墮落天使即守望者，教人禁術，生下巨人。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Tagging the sons of God with divine-marriage is an interpretive act comparing divine-human unions across traditions; the giant tag follows the LXX/traditional reading of Nephilim as giants, noted here.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them, that the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose. And the LORD said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.

There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown. And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.

region.en: The ark, resting on the mountains of Ararat

texts.period: Genesis 6-9, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 6-9

summary.en: God, grieved that every imagination of the human heart is evil, resolves to destroy all flesh with a flood and commands the just Noah to build a three-deck ark of gopher wood. The fountains of the great deep break up, rain falls forty days, all life drowns except the ark's eight souls and their beasts; a dove bearing an olive leaf announces the dry land, and God smells Noah's sacrifice, vowing never again to curse the ground, sealing the covenant with a bow in the cloud.
summary.zh: 神見人心所思盡惡，決以洪水滅絕血氣；命義人挪亞造歌斐木三層方舟。大淵泉源裂開，天窗敞開，暴雨四十日，生靈盡滅，唯舟中八口與走獸得存。鴿子銜橄欖葉報干地，神聞馨香之祭，誓言永不咒詛大地，以雲中虹為永約之記。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of Christianity and Judaism. Presented as the canonical flood narrative of the cross-tradition deluge cluster — scholarly framing, not a claim about religious truth.

passages.text: And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. And it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart. And the LORD said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them. But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.

Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch. And this is the fashion which thou shalt make it of: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits. And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven. But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee. Of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive with thee.

In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened. And the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights. And the waters prevailed, and were increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark went upon the face of the waters. And the waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high hills, that were under the whole heaven, were covered. And all flesh died that moved upon the earth: and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.

And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the window of the ark which he had made: and he sent forth a raven, which went forth to and fro, until the waters were dried up from off the earth. Also he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground; but the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him into the ark. And he stayed yet other seven days; and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.

title.en: Noah's Vineyard and the Curse of Canaan
title.zh: 挪亞葡萄園與迦南之咒

region.en: Noah's tent after the flood, near Ararat foothills
region.zh: 洪水後挪亞的帳棚，亞拉臘山麓

texts.period: Genesis 9, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapter 9

summary.en: After the flood Noah plants a vineyard and lies uncovered in his drunkenness; Ham, father of Canaan, sees and tells his brothers, who walk backward to cover their father. Waking, Noah curses not Ham but Canaan — 'a servant of servants shall he be' — and blesses Shem and Japheth: an etiological curse giving Israelite victory over the Canaanites, later grievously misused; biblical scholars and churches now repudiate its later racial readings.
summary.zh: 洪水後挪亞栽葡萄園，醉臥失衣；含見父赤裸而告二弟，閃與雅弗倒退而進遮蓋之。挪亞醒後咒詛的不是含，而是迦南——「必作奴僕的奴僕」——並祝福閃、雅弗。此為解釋以色列戰勝迦南族的溯源故事；歷史上曾被曲解為種族主義之據，今為教會與學界所唾棄。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. This text's long history of racist 'curse of Ham' misreading is documented and rejected in modern scholarship; included as a boundary-marking curse narrative with that context made explicit.

passages.text: And Noah began to be an husbandman, and he planted a vineyard: and he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent. And Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, and told his two brethren without. And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward, and they saw not their father's nakedness.

And Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his younger son had done unto him. And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren. And he said, Blessed be the LORD God of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant. God shall enlarge Japheth, and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.

title.en: Nimrod and the Tower of Babel

region.en: Land of Shinar, plain of Babylon

texts.period: Genesis 10-11, primeval cycle, c. 6th-5th century BCE (KJV, 1611)

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 1: Genesis, chapters 10-11

summary.en: Nimrod, the mighty hunter before the LORD, founds Babel, Erech, Accad, and Nineveh — the beginnings of empire in Shinar. There the whole earth, still of one language, builds a city and a tower whose top may reach heaven, to make a name; the LORD comes down, confounds their speech, and scatters them abroad, leaving the place named Babel. Christian tradition reads the tower as humanity's imperial pride, and Pentecost's gift of tongues as its reversal.
summary.zh: 寧錄為耶和華面前的英勇獵戶，建巴別、以力、亞甲、尼尼微——示拿王國之始。當時天下人口音言語如一，遂築城與通天塔，欲揚己名；耶和華降臨，變亂口音，散眾於全地，遂名巴別。基督教傳統視此塔為人類帝國式狂傲，而五旬節方言恩賜即其逆轉。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. Included as a hubris-and-confusion etiology; the Pentecost reversal is noted as the Christian reading.

passages.text: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth. He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD. And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar. Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh.

And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech. And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth. And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded. And the LORD said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do.

Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another's speech. So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city. Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.
